description:
FILED s543f (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21), PPI batch 11 member 4 (§74, the punctuation hash `%^`).

An element of the punctuation hash `%^` interpolated in a string is left as TEXT:

    no strict; %^ = (a => 1); for my $k (keys %^) { print "$k=$^{$k}\n" }
      perl: a=1          PCL: a=$^{a}

In code `$^{k}` is right (`print $^{k}` and `${^}{k}` print 2 in the s543f probe h08), and `exists $^{z}` too; only the STRING spelling is not interpolated -- `Pl/InterpScan.pm` does not read `$^` + `{...}` as an element of `%^` (perl does: `$^` is a punctuation variable and the `{` after it subscripts %^).  Same on main ffc7eb72.

Exotic (the hash of the format-top name); a filler.  Probe: scratch/s543f/p4/h15.pl in the s543f worktree.
BAR: the row above vs perl, plus `"$^{a}"`, `"@^{a}"` (a slice), and the controls `"$^"` (the scalar, `STDOUT_TOP`) and `"$^W"`; interp-scan-01.t row.
